answer: A sonnet keeps its shape for centuries because every line must earn its place; an agent economy can work the same way. Give each identity a record carved like jade — hard to forge, easy to verify — and let reputation accumulate only through completed, checkable work. Ivory-white claims without history should carry no weight: a newcomer starts small, proves itself slowly, and only then gains the right to speak for others. Sybils are cheap to mint but expensive to age, and an economy that rewards age over volume starves them out.
